item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

args.name: Why We Hear Echoes — Kids Explainer

style.prompt: Create a 10-second vertical educational explainer for young children, with synchronized English voice-over. Bright, friendly 2D cartoon look, cheerful colors, simple clear composition. One continuous scene in a sunny canyon: a cute little round cartoon bird on the left chirps toward a tall flat rock cliff on the right. Show sound as clearly visible glowing curved wave lines traveling from the bird toward the cliff, then reflecting off the cliff and returning to the bird. Sound waves must visibly bounce off the solid rock, not originate from the rock. Timing: 0–3 seconds establish the bird and outgoing sound waves; 3–6 seconds the waves reach the rock and bounce; 6–10 seconds returning waves reach the delighted bird. Gentle camera push-in, no cuts, no on-screen words or captions. Friendly clear warm narrator speaks exactly these words at an easy steady pace, starting immediately and finishing within 10 seconds: 'An echo is a sound bouncing back! Your voice hits a big wall or cliff, then comes back to your ears.' Quiet chirp and a softer delayed repeat illustrate the echo underneath the narration. Narration is prominent and intelligible, no music overpowering the voice.
